observation.visible_scene: A fixed upward view of a partly cloudy sky. A large dark grey overcast cloud mass fills the top and upper-right of the frame; a bright white cumulus bank lines the bottom edge; a softer grey-white cloud layer sits on the right side; a band of clear blue sky separates the dark mass from the white cumulus, with a few small wisps at the left.
visible_changes: Over the ~2.7 s excerpt the cloud formations drift and deform only slowly and subtly: the lower edge of the dark overhead mass and the right-side grey cloud creep/reshape slightly relative to the white cumulus bank below, while the central blue-sky gap stays open throughout.
The bright white cumulus along the bottom remains largely in place, with its billowing edges changing shape marginally rather than translating across the frame.

No rapid motion, no object entering or leaving, and no visible editing cut; the framing of the cloud regions stays consistent, indicating the camera is essentially stationary and the changes are cloud motion/morphing.
The overall arrangement (dark mass above, white bank below, blue gap between) persists as a stable property across all frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: The true direction and speed of the cloud drift before the first frame and after the last frame.
Whether the dark mass is advancing, receding, or merely churning, and any later change in sky conditions.
uncertain_details: The drift direction and magnitude are very small and hard to pin down frame-to-frame; subtle shifts could partly reflect compression or slight camera instability rather than clear cloud translation.
Distinguishing slow horizontal drift from in-place deformation/boiling of the cloud edges is not fully resolvable at this sampling rate.
